findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed sanitizer bucket in kitchen to have a quaternary ammonia concentration of roughly 50ppm. PIC was informed and replaced the bucket, measuring 200ppm. It seemed like there were three working rags in the same bucket. Intensive use of the bucket can cause the sanitizer concentration to dilute quickly. PIC was advised to use more buckets if necessary to keep up with sanitizing demand.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment: Observed cheerios and waffle mix to be stored directly on the floor in the 2nd floor dry storage closet. PIC was informed that food items need to be stored a minimum of 6 inches off the floor to prevent cross-contamination. Ensure food is stored at least 6 inches off the floor by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.comment: Observed personal food items stored in the cooler with food for the facility. PIC was informed that personal food items pose a cross-contamination hazard for food for the consumer. Personal food items can be stored in the cooler, but they need to be stored either on the bottom shelf of the cooler or in a solid container to prevent cross-contamination. Ensure personal items are properly stored by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-403.11(B) Designated Areas. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES can not occur.
